title: autostart tests spawned real opencode serve — crashed CI (ENOENT), orphan risk locally
description: External review P0, verified: autostart.test.ts mocked only the health fetch; ensureOpencodeRunning still executed real spawn('opencode serve') per test. On CI runners without the binary the async error event had no listener -> uncaughtException, failing every CI run since ci.yml landed. Fixed: _setSpawn/_resetSpawn seam, fake spawner in tests, production error listener racing waitForHealth so ENOENT fails fast with a clear message instead of a 30s timeout.
close_reason: Fixed: spawn seam + error listener + 2 regression tests; 182/182

title: Self-update command installs wrong npm package (legate vs @momidala/legate)
description: src/cli.ts:40 and :48 generate the /legate-update skill card with 'npm install -g legate@latest', but this package is @momidala/legate. Unscoped 'legate' on npm is an unrelated third-party package ('a simple api framework') — running /legate-update installs it globally. Dependency-confusion hazard. Fix: (1) skill card install + update strings to @momidala/legate, (2) the embedded node -e version check requires 'legate/package.json' — change to '@momidala/legate/package.json', (3) cli.test.ts:510 asserts the WRONG name and must be updated. Ship as 2.2.4 promptly.
close_reason: Fixed unscoped package name in update command, version-check require path, skill card, and test assertion

title: Verify legate_await stale-busy heuristic does not return partial results on long tasks
description: index.ts:1329-1352: after 5 consecutive busy polls (~10s) legate_await breaks out if the last message role is assistant. If OpenCode persists assistant messages WHILE streaming, this returns partial output for any task longer than 10s. Empirically test: dispatch a >30s task, poll session.messages mid-run, check whether the in-progress assistant message is visible. If yes, tighten the heuristic to also require a terminal part (step-finish) or completed time.end on the last message.
notes: CONFIRMED empirically against live server (thor, ollama/qwen3-coder, session ses_0cc5ed4e1ffepBjQEZ3NsS0TsR): assistant message row exists with role=assistant and 0 parts from the instant prompt_async is accepted; info.time.completed absent while busy, set only at true completion (also finish='stop', step-finish part). Current heuristic (role===assistant after 5 busy polls = 10s) therefore fires on ANY task >10s and can return EMPTY results. FIX: in the stale-busy block require info.role==='assistant' AND info.time?.completed !== undefined. Apply after legate-epe lands (same code region). SDK type: AssistantMessage.time.completed optional, types.gen.d.ts ~98-127.
close_reason: Confirmed live: assistant message row exists from prompt acceptance; heuristic now also requires info.time.completed set, verified as the reliable completion signal

title: isSessionLive omits directory param — capacity check may prune live sessions
description: sessions.ts:142 liveness probe calls GET /session/:id with no directory query param. Every other OpenCode call threads directory because sessions are project-scoped. If the endpoint 404s for sessions outside the server default project, atomicCheckAndAdd marks live sessions dead and deletes them from sessions.json. First VERIFY empirically against an OpenCode server hosting 2+ projects; if confirmed, persist directory in SessionEntry and pass it in the probe (or use a non-scoped endpoint).

title: Unlocked read-modify-write on sessions.json loses concurrent writes
description: Only atomicCheckAndAdd takes the proper-lockfile lock. addSession (fork handler index.ts:604), removeSession (~15 stale-session cleanup paths), and the TTL-prune write inside readSessionMap (sessions.ts:101) all do unlocked read->write. Two concurrent Claude Code instances can interleave and lose entries (e.g. fork registration erased by concurrent prune). Fix: route ALL sessions.json writes through withSessionLock; move TTL pruning out of the read path into an explicit locked prune (e.g. during session registration). Read path should be side-effect free.

title: registry.ts migration guard checks directory existence, not file (same bug fixed in sessions.ts)
description: Commit 9d09fb0 fixed the prefect->legate migration guard in sessions.ts to check for the sessions.json FILE (dir is pre-created by the CLI, so a dir check silently skips migration). registry.ts:23 still has the original directory-existence guard, so servers.json can be left unmigrated. Fix: extract one shared migration helper (e.g. src/migration.ts) used by both modules, guard registry migration on servers.json absence, add regression tests mirroring sessions.test.ts _runMigration tests.

title: migration guard: check sessions.json existence, not directory existence
description:
FIXED in commit 9d09fb0 — filed for traceability.

Root cause: the one-time migration guard in src/sessions.ts checked whether ~/.config/legate/ (the directory) existed before copying from ~/.config/prefect/. The CLI command `legate add-server` creates that directory as part of its own setup, so on any machine where the user ran the CLI before the prefect→legate rename, the directory was already present — causing migration to be silently skipped even when sessions.json had never been written.

Fix: guard now checks SESSIONS_PATH (the file) instead of SESSIONS_DIR (the directory). Migration runs whenever sessions.json is absent, regardless of whether the parent directory exists.

Refactored into exported _runMigration(newPath, oldDir) for testability. Two regression tests added (tests 128–129).

title: prefect_abort should fall through to server endpoint when session not in sessions.json
description:
prefect_abort (and legate_abort via the MCP bridge) fails silently when the session ID is not found in local sessions.json — which happens after a context reset, crash, or any run where sessions.json got out of sync. The server-side endpoint POST /session/<ID>/abort works fine; the MCP tool just never reaches it.

Fix: prefect_abort (or a new prefect_force_abort) should fall through to the server HTTP endpoint when the local lookup misses, rather than returning an error or no-op.

Workaround until fixed:
  curl -X POST "http://localhost:<port>/session/<ID>/abort"

For a full zombie sweep:
  for port in 4096 4097 4098; do
    echo "=== $port ==="
    curl -s "http://localhost:$port/session/status"
  done

This is an upstream issue to file against @momidala/legate (prefect MCP bridge).
close_reason: Fixed: legate_abort now falls through to server HTTP endpoint when session not in sessions.json; fans out to all registered servers when no server param given

title: Consolidate LEGATE_/PREFECT_/OPENCODE_ env fallback chains into one resolveEnv helper
description: The deprecation fallback chain with per-var warn-once flags is hand-copied in index.ts (BASE_URL + timeout), config.ts, auth.ts, autostart.ts, sessions.ts (~200 lines + _resetWarnFlags hooks in each). Add resolveEnv(names[], opts) helper with one-time warnings; add resolveEnvInt with real validation (currently parseInt(v,10)||120000 silently turns LEGATE_TIMEOUT_MS=0 into 120s and accepts negatives — reject non-positive values with a warning). Also removes the dead warnedServerUrl/warnedOpenCodeUrl flags at index.ts:16-17 (they guard module-init IIFEs that run once anyway).

title: Extract shared tool-registration wrapper — collapse 40 duplicated handlers in index.ts
description: index.ts is 2078 lines: the stale-session error block repeats ~20x, the try/catch isError envelope 40x, D-12 string-match 4x. Add a registerSessionTool/registerServerTool higher-order wrapper handling: resolveServerUrl, 404 -> removeSession -> canonical stale-session error, JSON content envelope, catch -> isError. Each tool becomes ~15 lines of schema + handler body. Also unify tool-description drift (some say OPENCODE_DEFAULT_PROJECT, some LEGATE_DEFAULT_PROJECT — all should say LEGATE_DEFAULT_PROJECT with fallbacks). Estimated -600 to -800 lines. Blocked by typed OpenCodeApiError issue.
close_reason: Wrapper helpers extracted: 16 session-tools + 13 server-tools via wrappers, 11 custom keep shared helpers; index.ts 2066->1760; hermetic MCP stdio smoke test added asserting 40-tool contract; descriptions unified to LEGATE_DEFAULT_PROJECT

title: Introduce typed OpenCodeApiError; kill JSON-string error matching
description: Handlers throw new Error(JSON.stringify(error)) and callers detect 404s via .message.includes with '"status":404' / 'NotFoundError' (index.ts:361, 502, 1394). Fragile against SDK serialization changes. Fix: one throw site producing class OpenCodeApiError extends Error { status?: number; name?: string; raw: unknown }, callers use instanceof + .status === 404. isNotFound(index.ts:111) collapses into the class. Prerequisite for the tool-wrapper refactor.
close_reason: OpenCodeApiError with status/errorName/raw + isNotFound(); 45 throw sites converted; 3 string-match blocks replaced with instanceof; 8 new tests

title: Drop brittle exactly-40 tool-count assertions in index.test.ts
description: Three tests hard-code the tool count at 40, so every tool addition breaks three tests whose only remedy is editing the number. Keep the valuable invariants (zero prefect_ names; every registerTool name starts with legate_) and drop the exact-count checks — or derive the expected count from the skill-card table so there is one source of truth.

title: Add security warning to legate_inject_mcp_server tool description
description: legate_inject_mcp_server registers an arbitrary local command that OpenCode will spawn — a privilege-escalation vector comparable to session_shell, but unlike session_shell (index.ts:1867) and get_config (index.ts:1818) its description carries no WARNING. Add one: local configType executes an arbitrary command on the OpenCode host; only inject servers you trust.

title: File upstream OpenCode issue for status-map lag; link from legate_run grace poll
description: index.ts:334-345 adds an up-to-2s post-completion poll (8 extra HTTP calls per run) to paper over OpenCode status-map lag after stream close. File an upstream issue against opencode, add the link in the comment so the workaround can be deleted when fixed. Same underlying bug motivates the legate_await stale-busy escape — reference both sites.

Related: issues 32506, 27907, 17657; unmerged PR 14222 attempted same fix. title: postinstall fails on fresh-clone npm ci (build/cli.js does not exist yet)
description: Verified empirically while adding CI: a plain npm ci on a fresh clone exits non-zero because postinstall runs node ./build/cli.js install-command before tsc has produced build/. Published-tarball installs are unaffected (build/ ships in files array); only contributors and CI hit it. CI works around it with --ignore-scripts. Consider making postinstall resilient: node -e guard on existsSync(build/cli.js) or a || exit 0 wrapper, so a source checkout installs cleanly.
close_reason: scripts/lifecycle.cjs guard: postinstall/preuninstall skip cleanly when build/cli.js absent; verified plain npm ci on fresh clone now succeeds
